title: Naive conormal complex and normalized comparison data
statement: Fix standard polynomial cotangent coherence data $C$ [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data]. For a ring map $f:A\to B$, a presentation is a surjective factorization $A\to P\twoheadrightarrow B$. It is localized polynomial if $P$ is a localization of $A[E]$ on any set $E$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], compatibly with $A\to P$. Set $J=\ker(P\to B)$ and define the actual cochain complex $N(P)=[J/J^2\xrightarrow{d}B\otimes_P\Omega^1_{P/A}]$ in degrees $-1,0$, zero elsewhere, with $d([h])=1\otimes dh$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Use the canonical identifications of those terms; write $[h]$ for a kernel class and $b\otimes dx$ for a differential generator. A presentation map over a ring square $(\alpha,\beta)$ is a map $a:P\to P'$ commuting with base maps and augmentations. A naive map is a semilinear chain map $N(P)\to N(P')$ sending $[h]$ to $[a(h)]$ and $b\otimes dx$ to $\beta(b)\otimes d(a(x))$. The standard presentation is the degree-zero presentation of $C$. A comparison datum $\kappa$ over $C$ consists of these naive maps; existence of a lift from the standard presentation to every localized polynomial presentation; a chain projection $K(P^{\rm std})\to N(P)$ for every such lift $a$, given in degree zero by $b\otimes dx\mapsto b\otimes d(a(x))$ and in degree minus one by $b\otimes dx\mapsto b[a(d_0x-d_1x)]$; a derived comparison $L_{B/A}\to QN(P)$ equal to the image of every lifted projection; and an isomorphism $Q(\tau_{\geq-1}K(P^{\rm std}))\simeq QN(P)$ whose composite with the good-truncation projection is that comparison [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Here good truncation replaces degree minus one by the cokernel of its incoming differential and discards lower degrees. Require the derived comparisons to be natural for all localized polynomial presentation maps over arbitrary ring squares, restricting target coefficients along $\beta$. This defines comparison data and their normalization; it does not assert that such data exist or assert vanishing below degree minus one.
